policies.text: A 3.0 cumulative TCU GPA is required to declare a business major.
Business students below a 2.75 GPA after the first year must choose a major outside business.
Graduation with a BBA requires a 2.50 TCU cumulative GPA and a 2.5 major GPA.
Most finance prerequisites require a grade of C- or higher.

knownIssues.text: Real-estate electives on the Finance checklist are effectively closed to regular Finance majors: FINA 30313 is restricted to Finance–Real Estate concentration majors, and FINA 30623, 40603 and 40613 all require FINA 30313.
MANA 30350 (Strategy), required in the current business core alongside MANA 30250, is not in the TCU course list. BUSI 10153 and INSC 30863 are also missing.

Prerequisites in course descriptions differ from the checklists: FINA 30153 also needs ECON 10223 (C-); FINA 30203 needs ECON 10223 and 10233; INSC 30833 needs only INSC 30823; INSC 30853 and 40843 need only INSC 20263; INSC 40813 needs all four core BIS courses. The planner uses the course descriptions.

The INSC 30273 description says it substitutes for INSC 40843, which explains the substitution seen on audits. FINA 30233's description covers options and futures, matching the registrar title Financial Derivatives rather than the checklist title Investments II.
Many prerequisites are not courses: declared major, sophomore or junior standing, dean approval. The planner shows them on each course but cannot verify them.
The course list has no titles and no fall/spring offering pattern, so offering terms still come from the checklists or are assumed.

The Finance checklist lists Financial Modeling as FINA 30223 in the elective list but as FINA 30233 (the Investments II number) in its prerequisite list. The engine uses FINA 30223, which matches the catalog.

Upper-level and TCU-hour minimums differ between checklist versions (36/45 vs 42/58). The engine applies 36/45 only to students entering Summer 2025 or later; which version governs which catalog year is an assumption to confirm.
FINA 40623 appears both as a finance elective and as a global-content option. Whether one course may satisfy both is not stated, so the engine does not double-count it.
Most courses have no published fall/spring pattern in loaded sources; they are treated as offered both terms and labeled 'assumed'.
Section times are synthetic. Purple Schedule Builder requires two-factor sign-in and was not connected.

Course titles differ between sources: the registrar's audit lists FINA 30203 as Financial Institutions and FINA 30233 as Financial Derivatives, while the checklist and catalog list Money and Banking and Investments II.
Audits for a Fall 2024 requirement term apply 42 upper-division hours, 58 residency hours and a 37-hour business core, which matches the earlier checklist rather than the current one.

Rules seen on the audit but not modeled in the catalog planner: 6 Writing Emphasis hours taken at TCU, one HMVV category per course, at most 2 Human Experiences courses per subject, and a 120–135 total-hour band.
Advisor substitutions appear on the audit as courses 'directed' to a requirement line. The audit importer honors them; the catalog planner cannot see them.

BBA Core Reqs.name: Lower-Division Requirements & Business Core (all majors)
BBA Core Reqs.who: All Neeley BBA students; 2.75 GPA to stay in business, 3.0 to declare a major.
notes: Applies to every Neeley BBA major. Source: Neeley major checklists (entered Summer 2025 or after), Neeley admission/progression pages and TCU catalog.

Lower-Division courses must be completed before upper-division business courses. Progression: minimum 2.75 cumulative GPA to remain in business; 3.0 GPA to declare a major; Excel and PowerPoint (Office 365) certifications required (students entering Summer/Fall 2026: Excel by Nov 11, 2026, PowerPoint by Apr 7, 2027).

Variations: the Finance checklist lists ECON 10233 under Associated Requirements instead of Lower-Division. Strategy is MANA 30350 on the Accounting, Finance, Management and Supply Chain checklists but MANA 40250 on the BIS, Entrepreneurship and Marketing checklists. TCU Core Curriculum (39-63 hrs) overlaps with ECON/ENGL/MATH here and is not itemized.

Credit by examination is not assigned a letter grade and does not count toward special recognition or honors.

ACCT.about: Financial strategy, problem-solving and ethical decision-making for individuals, organizations and nonprofits.

BIS.about: How technology and business strategy work together: AI, analytics and emerging technology to improve processes and decisions.

ENTR.about: Creating opportunities, solving problems and leading change, or starting a business from the ground up.

FINA.about: Financial decision-making, investment strategy and value creation across wealth management, financial analysis and more.

FIRE.about: The Finance major with a real-estate concentration, supported by the Center for Real Estate.

MANA.about: Leading teams, strengthening organizations and making thoughtful business decisions with integrity.

MARK.about: How brands connect with audiences through strategy, storytelling and insight, with focus areas in digital marketing, consultative selling and brand management.

SVCM.about: How products, information and relationships move through a global marketplace, and how to keep them moving efficiently.
